pages.text:
Mann Shah 
Oracle Interview Experience 
 
Round  1 - Online Coding Round. 
 I was given a coding question on Stack , there were English and Aptitude 
Mcq’s, and a REST API question. Luckily my internship project consisted of 
the REST API, I was able to solve it. 
The coding question all the test cases were passed and I think I did well in 
mcq as well. 
 
 
Round 2 - Technical Interview 1 (50-55 mins) 
(mode - offline) 
The interviewer greeted me good morning and directly asked me to explain 
the projects I had built. I explained to him the projects one by one from a 
broader perspective. 
He then asked me about the project that i had built in the internship that i 
had done recently. It was on Spring boot and Rest API’s. I explained to him 
the project in detail. Starting with the problem statement and the need of

the project for the company, I later moved on to the solution and explained 
the approach I used to solve it.  
He saw JUnit in my project and gave me 3 JUnit test and told in which 
order will the JVM execute these test , that is all concurrently or one by 
one? 
 
He then asked me what to design a calculator on paper and told me to 
write pseudo code and explain the reasons for the code i write accordingly. 
After I wrote the code we discussed it for some time and he asked me 
some questions regarding why I had done so. I answered the questions. 
 
He then moved on to core java concepts. He asked me whether I knew 
how to write a code for multithreading in java. I told him my primary 
language was C++ and had worked with Java only for 2 months and was 
aware of the concepts I had used in my internship project. He then asked 
me to explain to me what threads are, how threads work with JVM. 
After I answered the questions he told me there are 3 processes and 3 
threads, when the program is run, which thread will the JVM execute first 
and why? I was not sure about the answer but then i thought for a half a 
minute and answered with the reason that i had thought. He told me it was 
correct. 
He asked me what an ArrayList is in java,  what is a map, what is the 
difference between arrayList and map,what is the disadvantage of 
arrayList, in what cases we should use map. 
 
He then moved on to Data Structures. 
He made a Binary tree and asked me the inorder , preorder and postorder 
traversal for it, the recursive code and time complexity. I straight away gave 
him and for all the questions and he was satisfied. 
 
He then gave me a String ABACABA and told me to find the number of 
palindromic substring of length >1. here it would be ABA, ACA, BACAB and 
ABACABA. That is 4. I thought this was a little difficult. I gave him a brute 
force solution and then he told me to optimize it.

I gave him the recursive solution and then told we can memoize it to reduce 
the complexity. After explaining the approach he told me to write the 
pseudo code for it. I wrote the code and dry run it on the example he gave. 
He was satisfied with my code. 
 
Then we moved on to databases. He told me which database I worked 
with. I told him I had used both SQL and NoSQL in my projects. He asked 
me the difference between both and the advantages and disadvantages of 
both. He asked me the difference between DELETE and TRUNCATE, 
which one is faster and why? What are DML and DDL commands and tell 
me to give examples. He asked what is caching in the database, how 
indexing works, how indexing works with caching? 
He then gave me a table which was not even in 1NF form and told me what 
was wrong with it and told me to restructure the entire table. I was able to 
reduce it to 2NF form and luckily there was no transitive dependency after 
2NF in the table :). He then gave me 2 tables and asked me what's outer 
join, union and union all. And told me to write a query on it.  
 
He then asked me if there is no primary key defined in the table, does the 
database provide a default primary key? He then gave me another table 
without a primary key where he was updating an already existing value and 
asked me will I get an error or not? 
He was satisfied with all of my answers regarding databases. I think he 
grilled me a lot in DBMS as compared to the other interviewees. 
 
He then asked me whether I had questions for him.  I asked him 2 
questions based on  the PPT they had shown earlier. 
 
I thought the round was pretty intense and was not sure if I would be 
selected further as the interviewer had almost no reactions for all of my 
answers :/.

Round 2 - Technical + HR (20 mins) 
 
The interviewer was smiling and asked for my introduction. After which 
he said that's pretty good intro i've heard in a while.  
He then saw I had mentioned Gitlab CI/CD jobs in my internship 
project. He asked me what is a pipeline, what is CI/CD, what different 
stages are then in the pipeline, why are they necessary, where do you 
write the job. Luckily I had done this properly during my internship so I 
could answer him. 
He then saw JUnits as well in the same project. And asked similar 
questions like what is JUnit Test, the syntax of JUnit test and told me 
to write any test on paper. I wrote the same test I wrote in my 
internship 😂. As I had done JUnits just for writing tests for the code 
that I had written in the internship. 
 
He then asked me to rate myself in java out of 10. I tried to get away 
with an ambiguous answer saying the same thing I had said in the first 
round. He then asked me why Java over C++? 
I gave him various reasons and then he asked follow up questions 
based on my answer about how to use friend functions in java.  
I thought this question was a good one and I told him as there is no 
friend function in Java but we want to access the private members 
outside the class (as that's what friend functions do in C++). I gave it a 
thought for a minute and then answered and he smiled and moved on 
to the next question. He asked if there is multiple inheritance in java. I 
said no and asked the reason. (diamond problem). 
 
He then moved on to HR questions. He asked Why oracle? Where do 
you see yourself in 2 and 5 years? Do you wish to switch to 
management in the future?

Later he asked if I had any questions for him? I asked him 3 questions 
which he answered very patiently and smilingly. 
We even joked about something at the end. 
I think this round was pretty good and went well. 
 
 
Both of my rounds were finished before 11.30 in the morning. Within 
10-11.30 :). 
 
The results were out in the evening and luckily I was selected.
